core.title: Scaffold criteria from the chosen harness's catalog template
core.given: You need a given/when/then scaffold, or the typical layers, for a criterion whose harness has an entry in the stack's harness template catalog — drafting before any file exists, revising, or just looking it up.
core.when: You draft, generate, revise, or look up that criterion's scaffold or layers.
core.then: Start from the catalog entry harness -> {layers, given/when/then scaffold} for the criterion's harness (verbatim, from the stack's harness template catalog), replacing its placeholder values with the criterion's real ones.
prefer: For a harness with a catalog entry, scaffold the criterion from that entry — its layer list and the key shape of its given/when/then — rather than composing a shape from scratch.
Replace each template placeholder — example request paths and URLs, sample payloads, placeholder targets and metric names — with the criterion's real values as you scaffold.
Treat each template's layers as the layers the harness typically exercises — a default, not a mandatory declaration.
avoid: Leaving template placeholder values (example paths and URLs, sample payloads, placeholder targets, placeholder metric names) in a finished criterion.
Inventing an ad-hoc given/when/then shape for a harness that already has a catalog template.
core.why: A reusable scaffold per harness keeps criteria uniform and records which layers each harness typically exercises.
evidence: Each criterion's given/when/then uses the key shape of its harness's catalog entry.
Any layers stated for a criterion are consistent with the harness's typical layers in the catalog.
verification: Compare each criterion's given/when/then key shapes (the kinds present in given, when, and then) against the entry for its harness in the stack's harness template catalog (harness -> {layers, given/when/then scaffold}); any layers stated for a criterion must be consistent with that entry's layer list.
Take each catalog entry verbatim when comparing: an entry whose when is empty, or that carries no given block, defines the expected shape as-is — an absent block is not a mismatch.
Template layers are defaults, not mandatory declarations: the check does not require a criterion to state layers; when layers are stated, it checks only their consistency with the catalog entry.
The check covers key shapes and layer consistency; whether template placeholder values were actually replaced with real ones is author guidance and is not part of the check.

values: <each harness kind named in the stack's harness template catalog>
needs harness scaffold or typical layers

fires: Planner drafts a new criterion naming a cataloged harness kind before any acceptance file exists and needs its given/when/then scaffold.
Planner looks up the catalog to see which layers a particular harness kind typically exercises.
Planner changes a criterion's harness kind and must re-scaffold its given/when/then.
Tooling generates a criterion skeleton for a chosen harness from the catalog.
doesNotFire: Coder implementing production code against an already-authored acceptance.
Editing prose docs that neither use a harness scaffold nor need a harness's typical layers.
Choosing the harness code itself (governed by the harness vocabulary convention, not this template catalog).

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's harness template catalog for acceptance criteria: the set of harness kinds and, for each, the layers it typically exercises and its given/when/then scaffold, whose values are placeholders to be replaced (in the event template, the then expectation names the same topic as the when block). The core uses this catalog to decide which harnesses have a template, what their typical layers and key shapes are, which task terms match activation, and what the key-shape comparison compares against.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's harness template catalog for acceptance criteria: the harness kinds and, for each kind, the layers it typically exercises and its given/when/then scaffold, whose values are placeholders meant to be replaced with a criterion's real values.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No vocabulary key carries a per-harness criterion scaffold catalog: the idiom group covers code constructs (route handlers, gates, imports, nesting), and roles/roots/layout/suffix/urn/tooling describe structure and tooling, none of which can express 'for each harness kind, its typical layers and given/when/then template'.

neutralityNotes: The operative content of this convention is a data catalog, not a structural rule: the 13 harness kinds, their layer lists, and their given/when/then scaffolds (including placeholder values) are carried as stack data behind the proposed key idiom.harness_templates, and the core is parametric over that catalog, naming no harness kind, count, path, or stack. The layer names inside the catalog already use the neutral role names (presentation, application, domain, integration), so no roles.* key is needed. Places where bun.json named concrete kinds — the given clause, the task_term values, and fires examples (harness: http, a db harness, unit to e2e) — were generalized to 'a cataloged harness kind' and expand from the catalog at instantiation; the task_term fact expresses this with one parametric value so realized activation is no weaker. The catalog term id harness_template and its label are realization details (bunOnly). The sibling-convention reference in doesNotFire was generalized from 'the acceptance harness vocabulary convention' to 'the harness vocabulary convention'. bun.json declares no severity or disposition, so the core's verification adds none. Placeholder replacement (avoid[0]) is author guidance: the evidenced checks are key-shape and layer consistency only, and the core's verification says so explicitly.
